observations: Photo 0 shows the underside of a laptop palm rest assembly with visible connectors, screws, and a black plastic frame. The text 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'MARSHADAKH MULTULINKS' is watermarked on the image.

Photo 1 shows the front of the same palm rest assembly with a full keyboard and a large trackpad. The keyboard layout is QWERTY with function keys and macOS-specific keys (command, option, control, etc.). The trackpad is large and centered below the keyboard. A small green sticker with 'A1369' is visible on the bottom right corner of the trackpad.
The item appears to be a MacBook palm rest assembly, including keyboard, trackpad, and possibly Touch ID, as claimed.

The background in both photos is identical: a wooden wall, a TV screen showing a green sports field, and a small plant. This suggests the photos were taken in the same location, likely a shop or office.

claims.evidence: The model number 'A1369' on the sticker in photo 1 is for a MacBook Pro (13-inch, Mid 2012–2015), not a MacBook Air 2018. The 2018 MacBook Air uses model A1932. The photos do not show any visible model identifiers for a 2018 MacBook Air.
Photo 0 and photo 1 show the palm rest assembly with keyboard and trackpad, which is the component being sold.
Photo 1 clearly shows a large trackpad below the keyboard.

The photos do not show the internal components or the fingerprint sensor. The trackpad in photo 1 does not have a visible Touch ID button, which is typically located on the right side of the trackpad. The model A1369 does not support Touch ID, so this claim is likely false, but cannot be confirmed without internal inspection.
